subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should OpenClaw preserve parallel execution for distinct ACP child sessions and fix the launch-readiness/runtime boundary, or intentionally gate distinct ACP session starts to avoid ACPX/Claude startup races?
rationale: Current source, docs, and tests preserve different-session parallelism with only an explicit `acp.maxConcurrentSessions` cap, so serializing distinct ACP spawns would be a behavior/product change rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Preserve parallelism, prove readiness
options.body: Run a live ACPX/Claude two-spawn smoke and fix the confirmed ACPX/OpenClaw startup boundary without changing distinct-session concurrency semantics.

options.title: Gate distinct ACP starts
options.body: Serialize or throttle distinct ACP child session creation if maintainers accept lower parallelism as the supported behavior for ACP backends.

recommendation.title: Preserve parallelism, prove readiness
recommendation.body: Run a live ACPX/Claude two-spawn smoke and fix the confirmed ACPX/OpenClaw startup boundary without changing distinct-session concurrency semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent ACPX/runtime history makes this the best available routing owner for the product/runtime call.
